name: HC-SR04P ultrasonic distance sensor (3-5.5 V)
description: Ultrasonic rangefinder that times the echo of a 40 kHz burst: hold Trig high for 10 µs and Echo goes high for the sound's round-trip time (µs / 58 = cm). Measures about 2–400 cm at 3.3 V (about 450 cm at 5 V), ±3 mm. The 'P' version uses the RCWL-9610 controller and runs on 3–5.5 V, so on a 3.3 V supply its Echo output is 3.3 V and needs no divider. Sold as: HC-SR04P 3-5.5 V ultrasonic distance sensor module (RCWL-9610 controller, blue board, 4-pin header VCC, Trig, Echo, GND).
eli5: Squeaks a sound too high to hear and times how long the echo takes to come back, which tells your board how far away the nearest thing is.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3–5.5 V. Use 3.3 V on ESP32/Pico so Echo is 3.3 V logic

pins.name: Trig
pins.description: Trigger input: a 10 µs high pulse starts one measurement

pins.name: Echo
pins.description: Echo output: high for the round-trip time of the sound (µs / 58 = cm); swings to VCC

buildNotes: Power VCC from 3.3 V on an ESP32 or Pico: Echo then swings only to 3.3 V. Powered from 5 V, Echo is 5 V and needs a divider (e.g. 1 kΩ / 2 kΩ) before a 3.3 V GPIO.
Start a reading with a 10 µs high pulse on Trig, then time the high pulse on Echo: distance cm = µs / 58 (58.3 at 20 °C).
Leave at least 60 ms between readings so a late echo is not taken for the next one.
Range drops to about 400 cm on 3.3 V (450 cm on 5 V); objects closer than 2 cm are in the blind zone.
Aim at a flat, hard target of at least 0.5 m²; soft, small or angled objects may give no echo.

driver.code:
# HC-SR04P ultrasonic distance sensor (RCWL-9610 controller, HC-SR04 compatible GPIO mode),
# MicroPython driver.
# Datasheet behaviour: hold Trig high for at least 10 us; the module then sends eight 40 kHz
# pulses and raises Echo for the round-trip time of the sound.
# Distance: cm = high-time(us) / 58 (speed of sound 340 m/s; 58.3 at 343 m/s, 20 degC).
# Leave at least 60 ms between measurements so the last echo has died away.
# Runs on 3-5.5 V; Echo swings to VCC, so power it from 3.3 V on 3.3 V boards.
from machine import Pin, time_pulse_us
import time

US_PER_CM = 58.3      # 2 / 0.0343 cm/us (sound at about 20 degC)
MIN_CM = 2            # blind zone
MAX_CM = 400          # rated range at 3.3 V (about 450 cm at 5 V)


class HCSR04P:
    def __init__(self, trig, echo, timeout_us=30000):
        self.trig = Pin(trig, Pin.OUT, value=0) if isinstance(trig, int) else trig
        self.echo = Pin(echo, Pin.IN) if isinstance(echo, int) else echo
        self.timeout_us = timeout_us
        self._last = time.ticks_ms() - 60

    def pulse_us(self):
        """Echo high time in us, or None if no echo arrived within the timeout."""
        wait = 60 - time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), self._last)
        if wait > 0:
            time.sleep_ms(wait)
        self.trig.value(0)
        time.sleep_us(5)
        self.trig.value(1)
        time.sleep_us(10)          # trigger: at least 10 us high
        self.trig.value(0)
        t = time_pulse_us(self.echo, 1, self.timeout_us)
        self._last = time.ticks_ms()
        if t < 0:                  # -1: echo never went high, -2: still high at timeout
            return None
        return t

    def distance_cm(self):
        """Distance in cm (float), or None when there is no valid echo / out of range."""
        t = self.pulse_us()
        if t is None:
            return None
        cm = t / US_PER_CM
        if cm < MIN_CM or cm > MAX_CM + 50:
            return None
        return cm

    def distance_mm(self):
        cm = self.distance_cm()
        return None if cm is None else cm * 10

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from hcsr04p import HCSR04P

sensor = HCSR04P(trig={TRIG}, echo={ECHO})
while True:
    d = sensor.distance_cm()
    if d is None:
        print('out of range')
    else:
        print('D=%dcm' % round(d))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
